question: Does the April-June 2018 SEAFDEC/NFRDI landing-site report add species-resolved Bolinao evidence beyond the later 2018-2020 report?

method.summary: Reviewed the SEAFDEC/TD repository item, complete five-page NFRDI report, its page-2 reuse statement, and the related 2022 Bolinao 2018-2020 landing report. No local PDF, table image, raw landing dataset, or species-identification records were retained.
method.scopeFinding: The report covers Coron, Palawan; Masinloc, Zambales; and Bolinao, Pangasinan, for April-June 2018. Its methods summary says enumerators collected species-by-gear identification and length/weight information, but the published tables show landing center, gear, month, unloaded boats, catch, and sampled length-frequency totals without scientific names or species-level rows.
method.reuseFinding: The report permits whole or partial reproduction in any form for educational or non-profit purposes with acknowledgement. Resale or other commercial use requires prior written permission from the SEAFDEC Secretary-General. No app-specific permission or determination that Bangwit's use qualifies for the conditional permission was established.

publication.title: Report of Fisheries Data Collection on Fish Landing Sites in Palawan, Zambales And Pangasinan, Philippines during April – June 2018
publication.publisher: Southeast Asian Fisheries Development Center, Training Department
publication.citation: NFRDI/Philippines. (2018). Establishment and Operation of a Regional System of Fisheries Refugia in the South China Sea and Gulf of Thailand, Report of Fisheries Data Collection on Fish Landing Sites in Palawan, Zambales And Pangasinan, Philippines during April–June 2018. Southeast Asian Fisheries Development Center, Training Department, Samut Prakan, Thailand; FR/REP/PH15, 5 p.
publication.accessStatus: Institutional repository metadata and complete five-page PDF reviewed online on 2026-11-19.

relatedSurveyLineage.relationship: Both are NFRDI/SEAFDEC Fisheries Refugia project landing reports for Bolinao and share an observation period in 2018. The April-June 2018 report may be subsumed by the 2018-2020 report, but record-level overlap was not verified.

reuse.licenseAsPrinted: The publication may be reproduced in whole or in part and in any form for educational or non-profit purposes with acknowledgement. Resale or any other commercial purpose requires prior written permission.

internalConsistency.issue: The report says the second-quarter catch increased by about 100 kilograms from the previous quarter but refers to the 'last quarter of 2018,' which is later than April-June 2018.
internalConsistency.disposition: Preserve this as a source date/wording inconsistency; do not infer which prior quarter was intended.

internalConsistency.issue: The activity summary describes the highest Coron bagnet catch as occurring in February although the report's stated collection period is April-June 2018.
internalConsistency.disposition: Do not use the February claim as a dated second-quarter observation; source clarification is needed.

internalConsistency.issue: The report says species identification was collected by gear type, but its published Bolinao table contains only landing-center/gear/month/boat/catch/length-frequency fields and no fish names.
internalConsistency.disposition: Treat species identification as an activity described by the report, not as species evidence contained in the reviewed table. Do not infer names from landing gear or sample counts.

internalConsistency.issue: The related 2022 report summarizes Bolinao landings over 2018-2020, so its totals may include the quarter reported here.
internalConsistency.disposition: Keep the reports linked but do not sum their totals or count them as independent sampling until source-level lineage is confirmed.

interpretation: This is fisheries-monitoring metadata for three municipal sites, not a species inventory. It adds landing-center names and quarterly aggregate effort/catch information but no scientific name rows.

The Bolinao table explicitly names Arosan and Binabalian as landing centers, not capture sites or waterbody polygons. Do not map those labels to a particular waterbody without independent locality evidence.

Although the methods summary says species-by-gear identification was collected, the reviewed publication does not expose that species-resolved dataset. The report's landing and length-frequency counts cannot be used as occurrence or species-abundance records.
The report's educational/non-profit reuse permission is conditional; commercial reuse requires written permission. Bangwit publication approval remains false.
No fish names, catch events, species assertions, waterbody assignments, geometry, raw data, or public-app rows were added. Region I and Luzon remain incomplete.
nextAction: Seek the underlying species-by-gear NSAP extract or a separate published Bolinao checklist with explicit reuse terms and capture/locality resolution. Treat the two SEAFDEC reports as potentially overlapping project outputs until their data lineage is checked.
